name: Lazarus Pharmaceuticals Hemolytic Suspension Matrix
description:
The Hemolytic Suspension Matrix is a synthetic blood substitute delivered via pressurized IV canister, designed to temporarily replace lost blood volume and oxygen-carrying capacity in patients experiencing severe hemorrhagic shock. Unlike earlier saline-based volume expanders, the Matrix uses a proprietary suspension of ferro-organic oxygen carriers — microscopic lipid-shelled particles that bind and release oxygen with approximately 60% the efficiency of natural hemoglobin. A single 500ml canister can sustain basic organ function in a patient who has lost up to 40% blood volume for a window of three to five hours.

Lazarus engineered the Matrix with field triage as its primary use case, which means the delivery system is deliberately idiot-proof: a pre-calibrated auto-injector reads the patient's estimated weight via a grip-sensor and adjusts flow rate accordingly, preventing the pulmonary edema risk that plagued earlier rapid-infusion systems. The suspension fluid itself is shelf-stable at ambient temperature for up to two years and is universally compatible — no blood typing required. The trade-off is metabolic cost: extended use beyond the safe window causes the ferro-organic carriers to fragment into compounds that require liver processing, and patients who rely on the Matrix too long face a narrow but serious risk of synthetic hepatotoxicity.

On the street, the Matrix is called 'The Embalmer' with dark affection — it keeps you looking alive long enough to either reach a surgeon or make peace with the alternative. Lazarus's marketing materials have never once acknowledged this nickname.

specifications.hepatotoxicity_threshold: Risk onset after 2 consecutive canisters without surgical intervention

tactical_use: Administered immediately upon identification of hemorrhagic shock in the field. The auto-injector can be operated by a non-medic with minimal training — two seconds of grip contact, locate a major vein, inject. Used to buy time for extraction or field surgery rather than as a standalone cure. Experienced medics pair the Matrix with the Lazarus Coagulant Bloom Injector to simultaneously address volume loss and active bleeding. Stacking multiple canisters is a known desperation measure with understood consequences.
cultural_context: The Matrix's universal compatibility and low price point have made it genuinely ubiquitous — it's found in household first-aid kits in middle wards, in every corporate security team's loadout, and in the back pockets of fixers who work dangerous meetings. Its accessibility is one of Lazarus Pharmaceuticals' most effective pieces of soft branding: the company that keeps GLMZ alive, canister by canister. Critics note that Lazarus simultaneously holds patents on the primary hepatotoxicity treatment for Matrix overuse, a conflict of interest that has never successfully been litigated.
known_users: Anyone who works in a profession with a high probability of getting shot
story_hooks: A counterfeit Matrix canister batch has hit the market — the suspension fluid looks identical but lacks the ferro-organic carriers, delivering nothing but saline while the patient's condition continues to deteriorate.

Lazarus Pharmaceuticals has quietly reformulated the Matrix to accelerate hepatotoxicity onset, increasing demand for their proprietary treatment — a whistleblower needs the original formula smuggled out before the new version reaches distribution.

A player character discovers that someone they were supposed to protect has been surviving on stacked Matrix canisters for three days straight — they're still walking, still talking, but the liver failure window is hours away.
An outer ward community has organized a Matrix stockpile as a mutual aid resource — Lazarus's legal team is contesting their bulk purchase rights under a newly filed distribution exclusivity clause.

physical_description.visual_profile: A compact, medical-grade pressurized canister topped with an integrated auto-injector mechanism. The form resembles a high-end aerosol inhaler crossed with a pharmaceutical delivery system — utilitarian and clinical, but engineered for one-handed emergency deployment. The canister body is rigid and cylindrical with a slightly tapered grip zone.
physical_description.dimensions: Approximately 15cm tall, 5cm diameter at widest point — slightly larger than a standard spray deodorant canister, designed to fit inside an emergency medical pouch or duty belt holster.
physical_description.weight_description: 0.9kg total (canister plus injector assembly) — handheld, easily carried in a medical rig or jacket pocket; noticeable but not burdensome.
physical_description.primary_material: Aircraft-grade aluminum alloy body with medical-grade polycarbonate pressure gauge housing and injection mechanism.
physical_description.finish: Matte anodized aluminum with a subtle brushed texture to prevent slipping during emergency use. The polycarbonate gauge window is semi-translucent with faint UV reactive elements.
physical_description.color_scheme: Clinical silver-grey primary body with accent striping in Lazarus's signature teal-blue. Pressure gauge dial face features black numerals on white with a red warning threshold line. Injectable tip is metallic gunmetal.
physical_description.interface_elements: Pressure gauge with rotating dial (0–500ml capacity indicator), tactile grip-sensor pad on the barrel (reads patient weight via brief contact), safety release lever (slide-to-unlock), and a single illuminated status indicator (green = ready, amber = partial pressure, red = expired/compromised). Injection port at canister tip is standard 18-gauge IV-compatible.
distinctive_features: Rotating capacity dial that visibly depletes as suspension is dispensed
Grip-sensor technology that auto-calibrates flow rate — displays estimated patient weight on micro LCD (1cm x 0.5cm) mounted on barrel
Safety lever with tactile 'click' feedback that prevents accidental discharge
Faint holographic Lazarus Pharmaceuticals seal on the canister body that changes color under different light angles
Pressure relief valve marked with a small Φ symbol (QUANTA pricing indicator)
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Embossed 'LAZARUS MEDICAL DEVICES' across top band. Smaller text: 'HEMOLYTIC SUSPENSION MATRIX | Lot/Expiry Date' printed on lower body. Regulatory compliance stamps: GLMZ Medical Authority approval seal, ISO emergency medical standard markings, and biohazard symbol (faint amber).
physical_description.condition_typical: Used units show micro-scratches on the aluminum from field rig contact and fingerprints on the polycarbonate gauge window. Pressure indicator needle will visibly recede after use. Grip sensor shows minimal wear but may have residual organic matter from patient contact — always wiped clean between uses.

image_prompt: Product photography of a Lazarus Pharmaceuticals Hemolytic Suspension Matrix canister on a stainless steel medical workbench. Dramatic overhead lighting casts sharp shadows. The canister is positioned at a 45-degree angle, pressure gauge facing camera. Teal-blue accent stripes glow subtly under cool LED work lights. Blurred syringe and surgical instruments in the background suggest emergency medical context. Shallow depth of field isolates the device.
